newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - finishes slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - finishes slightly lower.

text.p: U.S. municipal prices ended Friday's session unchanged to slightly lower, after losing early gains to profit taking in the Treasury market.

The market had been as much as 3/8 to 1/2 point higher following release of the October employment report early in the day, which bolstered analysts' view that the economy is expanding but not at an inflationary pace.
But profit taking pushed the government long bond 14/32 lower at 100-29/32, to yield 6.68 percent heading into the New York close.
In the muni secondary, bids on Chicago Park District MBIA 5.6s of 2021 were two basis points lower at 5.82 percent. Denver Airport MBIA 5-1/2s of 2025 were up one basis point to 5.76 percent.
In futures, the December municipal contract lost 9/32 at 115-19/32 while December T-bonds fell 8/32 to 112-24/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 91 ticks from 92 ticks at the close Thursday.
Next week's supply is expected to ease dramatically from the more than $5 billion of deals priced this week.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $2.5 billion in 85 offerings for the week, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $519 million in 46 offerings. The largest issue is a $136 million New York City new money and refunding taxable bond offering.
Negotiated sales total $2 billion in 39 offerings. The largest issue is an $822 million New York City tax-exempt general obligation issue through Bear Stearns & Co.
With the national election as the main focus for the week, munis are expected to tread lightly until the results are available.
"It'll be tiptoeing around, not much activity," one trader said.
